newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Army promotes first woman to 3-star general.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Army promotes first woman to 3-star general.

text.p: The U.S. Army on Tuesday made Lt.-Gen. Claudia Kennedy, an intelligence expert, the service's first woman three-star general.
"Well done ... well deserved ... and it's about time," Army Secretary Togo West said at Lt.-Gen. Kennedy's promotion ceremony at the Pentagon.
The promotion makes Kennedy the senior intelligence official in the Department of the Army.
Kennedy, who joined the Army in 1969, said at the ceremony, "It was the character and integrity of soldiers that made me want to be a professional soldier."

When Kennedy began her military career, she served in the separate Women's Army Corps at a time when women were not allowed to command male soldiers or advance beyond the grade of colonel, the Army said in a statement.
She became an intelligence officer in 1975 and most recently served as the Army's assistant deputy chief of staff for intelligence at the Pentagon.
The Marine Corps has had a three-star woman general since Sept. 1 of last year; Lt.-Gen. Carol Mutter is deputy chief of staff-Manpower and Reserve Affairs.
